headline: Gulf Fund Signals US$22m for 150-Bed Tash-Kömür Hospital; Site and Design First
dek: The Ministry of Health says a new multi-profile hospital would replace the ageing Soviet-era wards of the Lower Naryn district hospital, though nothing has yet been signed.
ticker: Gulf fund signals US$22m for new 150-bed hospital at Tash-Kömür
paragraphs: A Gulf development fund has indicated that it will provide US$22 million, about 185 million som at the official rate, toward a new multi-profile hospital of roughly 150 beds at Tash-Kömür, the Ministry of Health said on 23 November. The plan was presented at the Lower Naryn District administration by Health Minister Dr Jamila Kubatova and district head Alisher Kholmatov.

The new hospital would replace the wards of the Lower Naryn district hospital, much of which dates from the Soviet years. The ISEZ would pay for site works and design from the 2027 budget, which goes to the Mejlis this month.

The ministry was careful about what is and is not settled. Only an exchange of letters has taken place. No agreement has been signed, and no start date, contractor or final cost has been published. The split between loan and grant has not been made public either.

"A letter is not a contract, and we will not pretend otherwise," Dr Kubatova said. "The site and the design come first. When those are ready, the partner will have something solid to put its money into."

Mr Kholmatov called the project a gain for both care and work in the district. "People in Lower Naryn have waited a long time for a hospital that matches the size of the district," he said. "It would also bring skilled jobs to Tash-Kömür."

The need is plain on the road. Serious surgical cases from Lower Naryn and Iyık Janyl still travel to the Talas Regional Hospital, about seven hours away. Dr Yosep Temirkulov, the hospital's chief physician, said the referrals weigh on his wards. "Every patient who can be treated closer to home saves hours for the family and frees a bed here," he said.

Ministry officials linked the proposal to the Lieutenant Governor's health agenda. They pointed to the 24 new ambulances delivered on 16 November to the Regional Hospital and the rural health posts. They also pointed to this autumn's insulin shortages, which they said show why southern patients need more care within reach.
The 2027 budget debate in the Mejlis will show how much money is set aside for site works and design. The ministry said it will publish details once an agreement has been signed.
